messages.subject: Group SEM  Error
parts:
Hello!

I try to run a group SEM. There is no missing values in the data. The SEM runs well without group variables. I try it in many ways but lavaan shows an error:

 

Attempt 1:

SexModel <- eqMI.semtest(model = Model3a, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020, group = "Genero", meanstructure = TRUE, estimator = "MLR")
Error in Sigma.hat[[g]] : subscript out of bounds

 

Attempt 2: 

> semModel <- eqMI.main(model = Model3a, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020, group = "Genero", output = "both", equivalence.test = FALSE, adjRMSEA = TRUE, projection = TRUE, bootstrap = FALSE)

Error in as.character.default(x) : no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector

Attempt 3: 

 fit <- sem(Model3a,
+            data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020,
+            group = "Genero")
Error in Sigma.hat[[g]] : subscript out of bounds

I don't know why this happens.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Group SEM Error
parts: I have no idea what's wrong with syntax.

The problem is when you don't assign a different name to the object used to store the sem() results.

Model3a <- sem(Model3a, ...)

So when you pass Model3a (also Model3b) to eqMI.main(), it gives you the error that a lavaan object (of S4 class) cannot be coerced to a character vector (which is what your model syntax must be).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Group SEM Error
parts:
The error Terrence brought your attention to was that you replaced Model3b (the syntax) with Model3b (the lavaan object that is the result of the sem() call). So the syntax is no longer available when you get to the eqMI calls.

So change:
Model3b<- sem(Model3b, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020, meanstructure = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", mimic = "Mplus")

to

Model3b.fitted <- sem(Model3b, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020, meanstructure = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", mimic = "Mplus")

Model3b<- sem(Model3b, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020, meanstructure = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", mimic = "Mplus")

to

Model3b.fitted <- sem(Model3b, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020, meanstructure = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", mimic = "Mplus")

El domingo, 1 de noviembre de 2020 a las 6:50:24 UTC-4, Terrence Jorgensen escribió:
I have no idea what's wrong with syntax.

The problem is when you don't assign a different name to the object used to store the sem() results.

Model3a <- sem(Model3a, ...)

So when you pass Model3a (also Model3b) to eqMI.main(), it gives you the error that a lavaan object (of S4 class) cannot be coerced to a character vector (which is what your model syntax must be).
